exercises.question: Dejó de preocuparse por el determinismo después de leer la literatura compatibilista.
exercises.answer: She stopped worrying about determinism after reading the compatibilist literature.

exercises.question: El concepto se cree que se originó en la filosofía griega antigua.
exercises.answer: The concept is thought to have originated in ancient Greek philosophy.

exercises.question: Intentó aplicar el marco utilitarista, pero los resultados fueron contradictorios.
exercises.answer: He tried applying the utilitarian framework, but the results were counterintuitive.

exercises.question: She claims to discover a flaw in Aristotle's logic.
exercises.answer: She claims to have discovered a flaw in Aristotle's logic.
exercises.explanation: Cuando la acción ya ocurrió: 'claim + to have + pp'.

exercises.question: He regrets to publish his early conclusions before completing the full study.
exercises.answer: He regrets having published his early conclusions before completing the full study.
exercises.explanation: 'Regret + having + pp' = arrepentimiento por algo ya hecho.

exercises.question: The manuscript is believed to write anonymously in the seventeenth century.
exercises.answer: The manuscript is believed to have been written anonymously in the seventeenth century.
exercises.explanation: Pasiva con infinitivo perfecto: 'is believed + to have been + pp'.

exercises.question: Remember citing your primary sources whenever you present a philosophical claim.
exercises.answer: Remember to cite your primary sources whenever you present a philosophical claim.
exercises.explanation: 'Remember + to-infinitivo' = recordar hacer algo pendiente.

exercises.question: She stopped to worry about determinism after reading the compatibilist literature.
exercises.answer: She stopped worrying about determinism after reading the compatibilist literature.
exercises.explanation: 'Stopped to worry' = se detuvo para preocuparse; el sentido correcto es 'stopped worrying'.

exercises.question: He seems to understand the paradox when he first read it as a student.
exercises.answer: He seems to have understood the paradox when he first read it as a student.
exercises.explanation: Cuando la comprensión ocurrió en el pasado: 'seem + to have + pp'.

exercises.question: Working as a moral philosopher means to accept that many questions resist definitive answers.
exercises.answer: Working as a moral philosopher means accepting that many questions resist definitive answers.
exercises.explanation: 'Mean + gerund' = implicar / involucrar.

exercises.question: She tried changing her approach, but she did not succeed to convince the committee.
exercises.answer: She tried to change her approach, but she did not succeed in convincing the committee.
exercises.explanation: 'Try + to-infinitivo' = esforzarse; 'succeed in + gerund'.

exercises.question: The theory turns out more influential than critics had acknowledged.
exercises.answer: The theory turned out to have been more influential than critics had acknowledged.
exercises.explanation: 'Turned out + to have been' indica algo verdadero retrospectivamente.

exercises.question: He went on working on the argument and eventually concluded it was flawed.
exercises.answer: He went on to conclude that the argument was fundamentally flawed.
exercises.explanation: 'Go on + to-infinitivo' = pasar a hacer algo diferente.

exercises.question: The philosopher appears ___ (derive) this idea from Hegel rather than from Kant.
exercises.answer: to have derived

exercises.question: She remembered ___ (read) a similar argument in a journal article published the previous year.
exercises.answer: reading

exercises.question: I regret ___ (tell) you that this argument contains a fundamental logical fallacy.
exercises.answer: to tell

exercises.question: He stopped ___ (question) the premises when he realised the entire framework was inconsistent.
exercises.answer: questioning

exercises.question: She tried ___ (reconcile) the two competing theories but concluded they were irreconcilable.
exercises.answer: to reconcile

exercises.question: The ancient manuscript is said ___ (write) by a philosopher who studied directly under Socrates.
exercises.answer: to have been written

exercises.question: Working as a philosopher means ___ (engage) seriously with positions you fundamentally disagree with.
exercises.answer: engaging

exercises.question: He went on ___ (develop) a more nuanced ethical framework in the second volume of his work.
exercises.answer: to develop

exercises.question: She seems ___ (misread) the central argument, based on her response to the first chapter.
exercises.answer: to have misread

exercises.question: The doctrine is thought ___ (originate) in the medieval period before being formalised during the Renaissance.
exercises.answer: to have originated

exercises.question: A pesar de las limitaciones del estudio, los hallazgos brindan información significativa.
exercises.answer: Notwithstanding the limitations of the study, the findings provide significant insight.

exercises.question: En la medida en que el diseño de investigación es válido, los resultados son fiables.
exercises.answer: Insofar as the research design is valid, the results are reliable.

exercises.question: A la luz de las evidencias presentadas, el comité permanece sin convencerse de la relación causal.
exercises.answer: In light of the evidence presented, the committee remains unconvinced of the causal relationship.

exercises.question: A diferencia de la investigación anterior, este estudio adopta un diseño longitudinal.
exercises.answer: Unlike previous research, this study adopts a longitudinal design.

exercises.question: Con respecto a la metodología, los investigadores eligieron un enfoque de métodos mixtos.
exercises.answer: With respect to the methodology, the researchers chose a mixed-methods approach.

exercises.question: El primero es más riguroso metodológicamente; el segundo tiene mayor validez ecológica.
exercises.answer: The former is more methodologically rigorous; the latter has greater ecological validity.

exercises.question: El primer ensayo produjo resultados poco fiables; el segundo también lo hizo.
exercises.answer: The first trial produced unreliable results; the second did so as well.

exercises.question: Tampoco el grupo de control mostró un resultado estadísticamente significativo.
exercises.answer: Neither did the control group show a statistically significant result.

exercises.question: El estudio es defectuoso en la medida en que depende de una muestra no representativa.
exercises.answer: The study is flawed inasmuch as it relies on a non-representative sample.

exercises.question: Los resultados son válidos siempre y cuando se mantengan las condiciones del protocolo original.
exercises.answer: The results are valid provided that the conditions of the original protocol are maintained.

exercises.question: The study is flawed inasmuch it relies on a non-representative sample.
exercises.answer: The study is flawed inasmuch as it relies on a non-representative sample.
exercises.explanation: 'Inasmuch as' requiere 'as'; sin él la frase es agramatical.

exercises.question: Notwithstanding to the limitations, the findings provide valuable insight.
exercises.answer: Notwithstanding the limitations, the findings provide valuable insight.
exercises.explanation: 'Notwithstanding' es preposición; no va seguida de 'to'.

exercises.question: The above conclusions are tentative. So the preliminary findings are.
exercises.answer: The above conclusions are tentative. So are the preliminary findings.
exercises.explanation: La inversión correcta con 'so' es 'So + auxiliary + subject'.

exercises.question: Neither the experimental nor the control group did show significant improvement.
exercises.answer: Neither the experimental nor the control group showed significant improvement.
exercises.explanation: Con sujeto negativo 'Neither...nor', el verbo no lleva auxiliar 'did'; se usa el pasado simple directamente.

exercises.question: She revised the methodology. So her supervisor has.
exercises.answer: She revised the methodology. So did her supervisor.
exercises.explanation: 'So + auxiliary + subject' debe estar en el mismo tiempo verbal (past simple → 'did').

exercises.question: The evidence suggests a casual rather than correlational relationship.
exercises.answer: The evidence suggests a causal rather than correlational relationship.
exercises.explanation: 'Causal' (referido a causa) no debe confundirse con 'casual' (informal/informal).

exercises.question: Unlike to previous research, this study focuses on long-term outcomes.
exercises.answer: Unlike previous research, this study focuses on long-term outcomes.
exercises.explanation: 'Unlike' es preposición y no va seguida de 'to'.

exercises.question: In contrary to previous findings, this study reports a significant correlation.
exercises.answer: In contrast to previous findings, this study reports a significant correlation.
exercises.explanation: La expresión correcta es 'In contrast to', no 'In contrary to'.

exercises.question: The study was peer-reviewed. The follow-up did so too.
exercises.answer: The study was peer-reviewed. The follow-up was too.
exercises.explanation: Con el verbo 'be', la ellipsis usa 'was/were', no 'did so'.

exercises.question: The data is conclusive in respect of that the hypothesis is supported.
exercises.answer: The data is conclusive with respect to the hypothesis being supported.
exercises.explanation: 'With respect to' es la expresión correcta; 'in respect of that' no es estándar.

exercises.question: ___ the findings of the first study, the second team reached entirely different conclusions.
exercises.answer: Unlike

exercises.question: The policy is ineffective ___ as it fails to address the structural causes of the problem.
exercises.answer: insofar

exercises.question: ___ respect to the sampling method, a stratified random approach was adopted.
exercises.answer: With

exercises.question: The results are valid ___ the conditions specified in the original protocol were maintained.
exercises.answer: provided that

exercises.question: The quantitative and qualitative approaches were both used; the ___ yielded richer narrative data.
exercises.answer: latter

exercises.question: Neither ___ the second cohort show any statistically significant improvement after the intervention.
exercises.answer: did

exercises.question: The first study found a significant correlation, and ___.
exercises.answer: so did the second

exercises.question: ___ the limitations acknowledged by the authors themselves, the study makes a valuable contribution.
exercises.answer: Notwithstanding

exercises.question: The findings of the 2019 study contradict ___ of earlier systematic reviews.
exercises.answer: those

exercises.question: The results are significant ___ as the sample size is sufficiently large to permit generalisation.
exercises.answer: insofar

exercises.question: Fue el periodista de investigación, no el gobierno, quien reveló el escándalo por primera vez.
exercises.answer: It was the investigative journalist, not the government, who first revealed the scandal.

exercises.question: No fue hasta que se publicaron los documentos filtrados que se conoció el alcance total del encubrimiento.
exercises.answer: It was not until the leaked documents were published that the full extent of the cover-up became known.

exercises.question: Lo que más preocupaba a los analistas era la ausencia de perspectivas alternativas en la cobertura.
exercises.answer: What had concerned analysts most was the absence of alternative perspectives in the coverage.

exercises.question: No solo las plataformas de redes sociales no eliminaron el contenido, sino que lo amplificaron activamente.
exercises.answer: Not only have social media platforms failed to remove the content, but they have actively amplified it.

exercises.question: Jamás antes el público había tenido acceso a tantas fuentes de información simultáneamente.
exercises.answer: Never before has the public had access to so many sources of information simultaneously.

exercises.question: Rara vez una sola historia ha tenido un impacto tan inmediato y duradero en la política pública.
exercises.answer: Rarely has a single story had such an immediate and lasting impact on public policy.

exercises.question: Lo que hizo el editor fue eliminar los párrafos críticos sin el conocimiento del periodista.
exercises.answer: What the editor did was remove the critical paragraphs without the journalist's knowledge.

exercises.question: Solo cuando se presentó el denunciante salió a la luz toda la verdad.
exercises.answer: Only after the whistleblower came forward did the full truth come to light.

exercises.question: Apenas se había publicado el informe cuando los periodistas empezaron a cuestionar su metodología.
exercises.answer: Scarcely had the report been published when journalists began raising questions about its methodology.

exercises.question: Solo cuando la evidencia fue verificada independientemente el editor aceptó publicar la historia.
exercises.answer: Only when the evidence had been independently verified did the editor agree to publish the story.

exercises.question: Not only the newspaper published the story, but it also ran an editorial calling for reform.
exercises.answer: Not only did the newspaper publish the story, but it also ran an editorial calling for reform.
exercises.explanation: 'Not only' al inicio requiere inversión: 'Not only + did + subject + base verb'.

exercises.question: It was not until that the story broke that the public became aware of the manipulation.
exercises.answer: It was not until the story broke that the public became aware of the manipulation.
exercises.explanation: La estructura correcta es 'not until + clause' sin 'that' adicional entre 'until' y la cláusula.

exercises.question: Scarcely had the interview ended when did the presenter receive a legal threat.
exercises.answer: Scarcely had the interview ended when the presenter received a legal threat.
exercises.explanation: Después de 'when' en esta estructura no hay inversión.

exercises.question: What the whistleblower done was expose a systematic pattern of editorial suppression.
exercises.answer: What the whistleblower did was expose a systematic pattern of editorial suppression.
exercises.explanation: La what-cleft usa el auxiliar correcto: 'what + subject + did + was'.

exercises.question: Never before the public had access to so many competing sources of information.
exercises.answer: Never before had the public had access to so many competing sources of information.
exercises.explanation: 'Never before + had + subject + pp': inversión con past perfect.

exercises.question: Rarely does a single article has such a significant impact on public discourse.
exercises.answer: Rarely does a single article have such a significant impact on public discourse.
exercises.explanation: Después de 'does' se usa la forma base del verbo: 'have', no 'has'.

exercises.question: No sooner the retraction had been published than further errors were discovered.
exercises.answer: No sooner had the retraction been published than further errors were discovered.
exercises.explanation: 'No sooner + had + subject + pp + than': la inversión va al inicio.

exercises.question: Only after the scandal broke, did the regulator launch an investigation.
exercises.answer: Only after the scandal broke did the regulator launch an investigation.
exercises.explanation: No hay coma antes de 'did' en las inversiones con 'Only after'.

exercises.question: What concerns analysts has been the growing influence of algorithmic curation on public opinion.
exercises.answer: What concerns analysts is the growing influence of algorithmic curation on public opinion.
exercises.explanation: La what-cleft en presente usa 'is', no 'has been'.

exercises.question: Only after the whistleblower came forward did the full truth came to light.
exercises.answer: Only after the whistleblower came forward did the full truth come to light.
exercises.explanation: Después de 'did' se usa el infinitivo sin inflexión: 'come to light', no 'came'.

exercises.question: It was not ___ the third investigation that the full scope of the misinformation campaign was uncovered.
exercises.answer: until

exercises.question: What ___ most about the coverage was the complete absence of contextual information for readers.
exercises.answer: had concerned

exercises.question: Not only ___ the platform failed to moderate the content, but it actively promoted it to users.
exercises.answer: had

exercises.question: Scarcely ___ the retraction been published when lawyers began preparing a defamation case.
exercises.answer: had

exercises.question: Only when the evidence was corroborated by multiple independent sources ___ the story published.
exercises.answer: was

exercises.question: ___ has a single piece of disinformation spread so widely in such a short period of time.
exercises.answer: Never before

exercises.question: No sooner ___ the correction appeared online than users began resharing the original false story.
exercises.answer: had

exercises.question: It was the lack of editorial oversight, not the journalist's error, ___ led to the scandal.
exercises.answer: that

exercises.question: What ___ audiences was not the misinformation itself but the speed at which it spread.
exercises.answer: had alarmed

exercises.question: Only by strengthening media literacy education ___ society become more resistant to manipulation.
exercises.answer: can

exercises.question: El gobierno hizo que expertos independientes realizaran el estudio de impacto ambiental.
exercises.answer: The government had independent experts conduct the environmental impact study.

exercises.question: La empresa hizo que su huella de carbono fuera auditada por un tercero.
exercises.answer: The company had its carbon footprint audited by a third party.

exercises.question: Ha salido a la luz que varias corporaciones habían falsificado sus datos de emisiones.
exercises.answer: It has come to light that several corporations had been falsifying their emissions data.

exercises.question: Se ha establecido que el gobierno conocía los niveles de contaminación años antes de actuar.
exercises.answer: It has been established that the government was aware of the pollution levels years before taking action.

exercises.question: Al parecer, la tasa de deforestación se había acelerado significativamente tras el cambio de gobierno.
exercises.answer: It would appear that the deforestation rate had accelerated significantly following the change of government.

exercises.question: La activista logró que el informe fuera traducido a doce idiomas para una distribución más amplia.
exercises.answer: The activist got the report translated into twelve languages for wider distribution.

exercises.question: Se entiende que la nueva política eximirá a las pequeñas empresas de los requisitos del impuesto al carbono.
exercises.answer: It is understood that the new policy will exempt small businesses from the carbon tax requirements.

exercises.question: Se alegó que el organismo ambiental había suprimido sus propios resultados de investigación.
exercises.answer: It was alleged that the environmental agency had suppressed its own research findings.

exercises.question: Las autoridades locales deberían hacer que se monitoree continuamente la calidad del aire cerca de sitios industriales.
exercises.answer: Local authorities should have air quality monitored continuously in areas near industrial sites.

exercises.question: Se ha argumentado durante mucho tiempo que la pérdida de biodiversidad representa una amenaza tan grave como el cambio climático.
exercises.answer: It has long been argued that biodiversity loss poses as serious a threat as climate change itself.

exercises.question: The city got the new green infrastructure to install by a local contractor.
exercises.answer: The city got the new green infrastructure installed by a local contractor.
exercises.explanation: 'Get + object + pp' para el causative pasivo; no 'to install'.

exercises.question: It was transpired that the environmental agency had suppressed its own research findings.
exercises.answer: It transpired that the environmental agency had suppressed its own research findings.
exercises.explanation: 'Transpire' en este sentido es activo; 'It transpired that' es correcto.

exercises.question: It emerges that the cap-and-trade scheme had been poorly designed from the outset.
exercises.answer: It has emerged that the cap-and-trade scheme had been poorly designed from the outset.
exercises.explanation: Para noticias recientes se usa 'It has emerged that' (present perfect).

exercises.question: It was understood the carbon offset scheme would be reviewed after the first compliance period.
exercises.answer: It was understood that the carbon offset scheme would be reviewed after the first compliance period.
exercises.explanation: La pasiva impersonal requiere 'that' antes de la cláusula subordinada.

exercises.question: It has long argued that biodiversity loss poses as serious a threat as climate change.
exercises.answer: It has long been argued that biodiversity loss poses as serious a threat as climate change.
exercises.explanation: La estructura pasiva requiere 'been': 'It has long been argued that'.

exercises.question: The factory had their pollution levels reduced by installing new filtration systems.
exercises.answer: The factory had its pollution levels reduced by installing new filtration systems.
exercises.explanation: El pronombre posesivo debe concordar con el sujeto singular: 'its', no 'their'.

exercises.question: The government got independent experts conducting the impact study before approving the project.
exercises.answer: The government got independent experts to conduct the impact study before approving the project.
exercises.explanation: 'Get + object + to-infinitivo', no 'get + object + gerund'.

exercises.question: It has come to light the climate data had been altered before publication.
exercises.answer: It has come to light that the climate data had been altered before publication.
exercises.explanation: 'It has come to light that' requiere 'that' antes de la cláusula subordinada.

exercises.question: She had the laboratory to analyse the water samples taken from the contaminated site.
exercises.answer: She had the laboratory analyse the water samples taken from the contaminated site.
exercises.explanation: Causative 'have + object + base verb': sin 'to' antes del infinitivo.

exercises.question: The activist got the documentary to screen at international film festivals to raise awareness.
exercises.answer: The activist got the documentary screened at international film festivals to raise awareness.
exercises.explanation: 'Get + object + pp': 'screened', no 'to screen'.

exercises.question: The government ___ an independent body ___ (audit) its carbon reduction commitments every two years.
exercises.answer: has / audit

exercises.question: It ___ (come to light) that the construction company had violated environmental regulations for over a decade.
exercises.answer: has come to light

exercises.question: It ___ (report) that methane emissions in the region have increased by thirty percent since the last survey.
exercises.answer: has been reported

exercises.question: The municipality ___ the entire river basin ___ (survey) after evidence of illegal dumping was discovered.
exercises.answer: had / surveyed

exercises.question: It is widely ___ that the transition to renewable energy will require significant investment in grid infrastructure.
exercises.answer: acknowledged

exercises.question: Environmental lawyers advised the community to ___ the soil contamination ___ (test) by an accredited laboratory.
exercises.answer: have / tested

exercises.question: It ___ (understand) that the new legislation will come into force at the beginning of the next financial year.
exercises.answer: is understood

exercises.question: The charity ___ the documentary ___ (screen) at environmental conferences to raise awareness.
exercises.answer: got / screened

exercises.question: It has long ___ (argue) that existing environmental law is inadequate to address the scale of the crisis.
exercises.answer: been argued

exercises.question: The firm ___ its supply chain ___ (audit) by a third party to ensure compliance with ethical sourcing standards.
exercises.answer: had / audited

exercises.question: Las sanciones se levantarán siempre y cuando el gobierno demuestre un cumplimiento verificable del tratado.
exercises.answer: The sanctions will be lifted provided that the government demonstrates verifiable compliance with the treaty.

exercises.question: Suponiendo que las conversaciones de paz tengan éxito, se establecerá un marco de alto el fuego permanente.
exercises.answer: Assuming the peace talks succeed, a framework for a permanent ceasefire will be established.

exercises.question: Aunque reconocemos los esfuerzos diplomáticos, la falta de mecanismos de aplicación sigue siendo una preocupación grave.
exercises.answer: Much as we appreciate the diplomatic efforts, the lack of enforcement mechanisms remains a serious concern.

exercises.question: Por más relevante que sea el progreso en las negociaciones multilaterales, las disputas centrales siguen sin resolverse.
exercises.answer: However significant the progress in multilateral negotiations may be, the core disputes remain unresolved.

exercises.question: Sea cual sea el enfoque adoptado por la comunidad internacional, deben abordarse las causas raíz del conflicto.
exercises.answer: Whichever approach is taken by the international community, the root causes of the conflict must be addressed.

exercises.question: En caso de que fracasen las negociaciones, la comunidad internacional podría recurrir a medidas económicas más duras.
exercises.answer: Should negotiations fail, the international community may resort to harsher economic measures.

exercises.question: El acceso a los beneficios comerciales permanecerá suspendido a menos que mejore la situación de los derechos humanos.
exercises.answer: Access to trade benefits will remain suspended unless the human rights situation improves.

exercises.question: La extradición procederá con la condición de que los tribunales de ambas jurisdicciones aprueben la transferencia.
exercises.answer: The extradition will proceed on condition that the courts in both jurisdictions approve the transfer.

exercises.question: El acuerdo se mantendrá en la medida en que todos los signatarios honren sus obligaciones bajo el derecho internacional.
exercises.answer: The agreement will hold as long as all signatories honour their obligations under international law.

exercises.question: Por más rígidos que sean los protocolos diplomáticos, no deben impedir una intervención humanitaria significativa.
exercises.answer: Rigid though diplomatic protocols may be, they must not prevent meaningful humanitarian intervention.

exercises.question: On condition of that the sanctions are removed, the government will allow UN inspectors access.
exercises.answer: On condition that the sanctions are removed, the government will allow UN inspectors access.
exercises.explanation: 'On condition that': no se añade 'of' a esta expresión.

exercises.question: Supposing if the agreement collapses, the region could return to open armed conflict.
exercises.answer: Supposing the agreement collapses, the region could return to open armed conflict.
exercises.explanation: 'Supposing' ya funciona como condicional; no necesita 'if' adicional.

exercises.question: Much as that the negotiations have been difficult, both parties have made substantial concessions.
exercises.answer: Much as the negotiations have been difficult, both parties have made substantial concessions.
exercises.explanation: 'Much as' no va seguido de 'that': directamente 'Much as + clause'.

exercises.question: However the situation may be dire, both sides must remain committed to dialogue.
exercises.answer: However dire the situation may be, both sides must remain committed to dialogue.
exercises.explanation: Con 'However', el adjetivo sigue inmediatamente: 'However + adj + subject + verb'.

exercises.question: Access to the humanitarian corridor will be guaranteed as long the ceasefire holds.
exercises.answer: Access to the humanitarian corridor will be guaranteed as long as the ceasefire holds.
exercises.explanation: 'As long as' necesita el 'as' final; sin él es agramatical.

exercises.question: Given that all parties would maintain their commitment, a lasting settlement may be achievable.
exercises.answer: Given that all parties maintain their commitment, a lasting settlement may be achievable.
exercises.explanation: Con 'Given that', no se usa 'would' en la cláusula condicional; se usa el presente simple.

exercises.question: The agreement will hold providing to that both governments honour their original commitments.
exercises.answer: The agreement will hold providing that both governments honour their original commitments.
exercises.explanation: La expresión es 'providing that', no 'providing to that'.

exercises.question: Notwithstanding of the economic costs, sanctions remain one of the few non-military tools available.
exercises.answer: Notwithstanding the economic costs, sanctions remain one of the few non-military tools available.
exercises.explanation: 'Notwithstanding' es preposición y no va seguida de 'of'.

exercises.question: The aid will be released so long the humanitarian corridors remain open and accessible.
exercises.answer: The aid will be released so long as the humanitarian corridors remain open and accessible.
exercises.explanation: 'So long as' necesita el 'as' final; sin él es agramatical.

exercises.question: The ceasefire will hold providing to that all armed groups lay down their weapons.
exercises.answer: The ceasefire will hold providing that all armed groups lay down their weapons.
exercises.explanation: 'Providing that' (no 'providing to that') = siempre y cuando.

exercises.question: ___ the ceasefire holds for ninety days, a joint peacekeeping force will be deployed.
exercises.answer: Provided

exercises.question: ___ the short-term political costs, the long-term benefits of engagement outweigh them.
exercises.answer: Whatever

exercises.question: ___ negotiations collapse, the international community has signalled it will increase economic pressure.
exercises.answer: Should

exercises.question: The treaty will remain in force ___ both governments respect the agreed legal procedures.
exercises.answer: as long as

exercises.question: The aid package will be released ___ that independent monitors are granted full access.
exercises.answer: on condition

exercises.question: ___ we acknowledge the complexity of the situation, a more decisive response is urgently needed.
exercises.answer: Much as

exercises.question: Access to funding will be suspended ___ the government implements the required institutional reforms.
exercises.answer: unless

exercises.question: ___ approach is taken, the international community must ensure that civilian populations are protected.
exercises.answer: Whichever

exercises.question: ___ that both parties remain committed to dialogue, a lasting peace agreement is achievable.
exercises.answer: Given

exercises.question: However ___ the diplomatic obstacles may be, the humanitarian imperative must take precedence.
exercises.answer: significant

exercises.question: La habilidad de persuadir sin mentir es la marca del retórico verdaderamente hábil.
exercises.answer: The ability to persuade without lying is the hallmark of the truly skilled rhetorician.
alternatives: The ability to persuade without lying is the mark of the truly skilled rhetorician.

exercises.question: Al apelar a la emoción antes que a la razón, el discurso distorsiona la deliberación democrática.
exercises.answer: By appealing to emotion rather than reason, the speech distorts democratic deliberation.

exercises.question: La pregunta no era inocente: llevaba implícita la presuposición de que él era culpable.
exercises.answer: The question was not innocent: it carried the implicit presupposition that he was guilty.

exercises.question: La diferencia entre persuadir y manipular reside en si el hablante respeta la autonomía racional del oyente.
exercises.answer: The difference between persuasion and manipulation lies in whether the speaker respects the listener's rational autonomy.

exercises.question: Encuadrar el debate en términos de crisis es una estrategia retórica deliberada para suprimir la disidencia.
exercises.answer: Framing the debate in terms of crisis is a deliberate rhetorical strategy to suppress dissent.

exercises.question: El lenguaje cargado de connotaciones convierte una descripción neutra en un acto de toma de posición.
exercises.answer: Language laden with connotations turns a neutral description into an act of taking sides.
alternatives: Language loaded with connotations turns a neutral description into an act of taking sides.

exercises.question: La concesión retórica — admitir la validez parcial del argumento contrario — es más eficaz que la refutación directa.
exercises.answer: The rhetorical concession — acknowledging the partial validity of the opposing argument — is more effective than direct refutation.

exercises.question: La repetición anafórica al inicio de cada estrofa crea un efecto de inevitabilidad que silencia la duda.
exercises.answer: The anaphoric repetition at the beginning of each stanza creates an effect of inevitability that silences doubt.

exercises.question: La subestimación deliberada puede ser más devastadora que la hipérbole: decir menos cuando se espera más.
exercises.answer: Deliberate understatement can be more devastating than hyperbole: saying less when more is expected.

exercises.question: El quiasmo invierte el orden de los elementos para hacer que la frase se grabe en la memoria del oyente.
exercises.answer: Chiasmus inverts the order of elements to make the phrase lodge itself in the listener's memory.

exercises.question: His argument was based on a straw man fallacy because he correctly represented his opponent's view before refuting it.
exercises.answer: His argument was based on a straw man fallacy because he misrepresented his opponent's view before refuting it.
exercises.explanation: Un 'straw man' distorsiona la posición del oponente, no la representa correctamente.

exercises.question: The speaker's appeal to the audience's emotions constituted a logos-based argument.
exercises.answer: The speaker's appeal to the audience's emotions constituted a pathos-based argument.
exercises.explanation: Las apelaciones emocionales son 'pathos'. 'Logos' apela a la razón y los datos.

exercises.question: A rhetorical question expects a detailed and thoughtful answer from the audience.
exercises.answer: A rhetorical question does not expect an answer from the audience — it makes a point through the question itself.
exercises.explanation: Las preguntas retóricas no esperan respuesta; su función es enfatizar o persuadir.

exercises.question: An ad hominem argument is considered effective in academic debate because it exposes the speaker's bias.
exercises.answer: An ad hominem argument is considered a logical fallacy in academic debate because it attacks the speaker personally rather than addressing their argument.
exercises.explanation: 'Ad hominem' ataca a la persona, no al argumento; es una falacia lógica.

exercises.question: Framing an issue as a 'public health crisis' rather than a 'personal choice' reflects a neutral, unbiased approach.
exercises.answer: Framing an issue as a 'public health crisis' rather than a 'personal choice' is a deliberate rhetorical choice that shapes how audiences perceive responsibility.
exercises.explanation: El encuadre nunca es neutral; cada elección de palabras implica una posición.

exercises.question: Hedging language in an academic argument signals intellectual weakness and should be avoided.
exercises.answer: Hedging language in an academic argument signals intellectual rigour — it accurately represents the level of certainty the evidence supports.
exercises.explanation: El lenguaje de atenuación en la academia es precisión, no debilidad.

exercises.question: A loaded term like 'freedom fighter' is more objective than 'guerrilla' because it avoids judgement.
exercises.answer: A loaded term like 'freedom fighter' is less objective than a neutral descriptor because it embeds a positive evaluation in the label itself.
exercises.explanation: 'Freedom fighter' está cargado de connotaciones positivas; no es objetivo.

exercises.question: Ethos is established primarily by using emotional anecdotes that help the audience trust the speaker's feelings.
exercises.answer: Ethos is established primarily through the speaker's demonstrated expertise, integrity, and credibility — not through emotional anecdotes, which appeal to pathos.
exercises.explanation: 'Ethos' = credibilidad del hablante; 'pathos' = apelación emocional.

exercises.question: The speaker used anaphora by ending each clause with the same phrase for emphasis.
exercises.answer: The speaker used epistrophe by ending each clause with the same phrase for emphasis.
exercises.explanation: Anáfora = repetición al INICIO; epístrofe = repetición al FINAL de cláusulas.

exercises.question: The phrase 'Live to work or work to live' is an example of antithesis.
exercises.answer: The phrase 'Live to work or work to live' is an example of chiasmus.
exercises.explanation: El quiasmo invierte el orden A-B / B-A; la antítesis yuxtapone ideas opuestas sin inversión.

exercises.question: The speech opened with three moving personal stories — a classic appeal to ___.
exercises.answer: pathos

exercises.question: Repeating 'This is what we owe our children' at the start of six consecutive paragraphs is called ___.
exercises.answer: anaphora

exercises.question: Describing the same policy as 'cutting waste' or 'gutting public services' shows how ___ shapes perception.
exercises.answer: framing

exercises.question: In academic writing, 'it would appear that' and 'the evidence suggests' are examples of ___ language.
exercises.answer: hedging

exercises.question: 'Not exactly the pinnacle of diplomatic subtlety' — describing a catastrophe this way is an example of ___.
exercises.answer: understatement

exercises.question: Attacking your opponent's character rather than their argument is the logical fallacy called ___ ___.
exercises.answer: ad hominem

exercises.question: A question with the correct answer embedded — 'Don't you think this policy has failed?' — is called a ___ question.
exercises.answer: leading

exercises.question: Acknowledging a valid point in the opposing argument before countering it is called making a ___.
exercises.answer: concession

exercises.question: Presenting only two options when many exist — 'you're either with us or against us' — is the fallacy known as a false ___.
exercises.answer: dichotomy

exercises.question: The appeal to reason through data, statistics, and logical cause-effect chains is called ___.
exercises.answer: logos

exercises.question: El narrador no confiable invita al lector a cuestionar no solo los hechos narrados sino la fiabilidad de toda perspectiva humana.
exercises.answer: The unreliable narrator invites the reader to question not only the narrated facts but the reliability of all human perspective.

exercises.question: La ironía dramática crea una distancia entre el lector omnisciente y el personaje ciego a su propio destino.
exercises.answer: Dramatic irony creates a distance between the omniscient reader and the character blind to their own fate.

exercises.question: El discurso indirecto libre borra la frontera entre la voz del narrador y los pensamientos del personaje.
exercises.answer: Free indirect discourse erases the boundary between the narrator's voice and the character's thoughts.

exercises.question: El motivo del espejo en el relato adquiere una carga simbólica que supera su función literal.
exercises.answer: The mirror motif in the story acquires a symbolic weight that exceeds its literal function.

exercises.question: La elección de la dicción — palabras latinas contra sajonas — refleja una toma de posición sobre la identidad lingüística del escritor.
exercises.answer: The choice of diction — Latinate versus Anglo-Saxon words — reflects a stance on the writer's linguistic identity.

exercises.question: El subtexto de la escena no está en lo que se dice sino en lo que deliberadamente se evita decir.
exercises.answer: The subtext of the scene lies not in what is said but in what is deliberately left unsaid.

exercises.question: La catarsis aristotélica supone que la representación de la tragedia purga las emociones peligrosas del espectador.
exercises.answer: Aristotelian catharsis supposes that the representation of tragedy purges the spectator's dangerous emotions.

exercises.question: El presagio narrativo sembraba desde las primeras páginas las semillas de un desenlace que el lector solo reconoce a posteriori.
exercises.answer: The narrative foreshadowing planted from the first pages the seeds of a denouement that the reader only recognises in retrospect.

exercises.question: La intertextualidad revela que ningún texto es una isla: cada obra lleva en sí las huellas de las lecturas del autor.
exercises.answer: Intertextuality reveals that no text is an island: every work carries within it the traces of the author's readings.

exercises.question: El personaje foil contrasta con el protagonista para hacer que sus rasgos sean más visibles por oposición.
exercises.answer: The foil character contrasts with the protagonist to make their traits more visible through opposition.

exercises.question: The author uses simile when she writes 'The city was a prison without bars'.
exercises.answer: The author uses metaphor when she writes 'The city was a prison without bars'.
exercises.explanation: Metáfora = afirma que algo ES otra cosa. Símil = compara con 'like' o 'as'.

exercises.question: Animal Farm is a metaphor for Stalinist Russia.
exercises.answer: Animal Farm is an allegory for Stalinist Russia.
exercises.explanation: La alegoría es sostenida y sistemática en toda la obra; la metáfora es una comparación individual.

exercises.question: Dramatic irony occurs when a character says one thing but means something completely different.
exercises.answer: Verbal irony occurs when a character says one thing but means something different; dramatic irony occurs when the audience knows something the character does not.
exercises.explanation: Ironía verbal = decir lo contrario de lo que se piensa; ironía dramática = el lector sabe algo que el personaje ignora.

exercises.question: In stream of consciousness, the narrative presents external events without commentary.
exercises.answer: In stream of consciousness, the narrative presents the unfiltered flow of a character's inner thoughts and feelings as they occur in the mind.
exercises.explanation: El flujo de conciencia captura el pensamiento interior, no eventos externos narrados objetivamente.

exercises.question: An unreliable narrator is always identified by the use of first-person narration.
exercises.answer: An unreliable narrator is not necessarily first-person; it is defined by the questionability of their account, which the text reveals through contradictions or gaps.
exercises.explanation: La no confiabilidad es una cuestión de perspectiva cuestionable, no de gramática narrativa.

exercises.question: The foil character shares the protagonist's most important traits and reinforces their strengths.
exercises.answer: The foil character contrasts with the protagonist's traits, highlighting them through difference rather than similarity.
exercises.explanation: Un foil resalta los rasgos del protagonista a través del CONTRASTE, no de la similitud.

exercises.question: Foreshadowing is a device used to create surprise by revealing information the reader had no hint of.
exercises.answer: Foreshadowing prepares the reader for later events by planting subtle hints — it reduces pure surprise in favour of dramatic anticipation.
exercises.explanation: El presagio prepara para eventos futuros; la sorpresa total requiere la ausencia de pistas previas.

exercises.question: A literary motif is the main theme of a text, expressed in a single sentence.
exercises.answer: A literary motif is a recurring element — image, symbol, idea, or phrase — that reinforces the text's themes; the 'main theme' expressed briefly is a thesis, not a motif.
exercises.explanation: El motivo es recurrente y concreto; el tema es la idea abstracta central de la obra.

exercises.question: Catharsis is the dramatic climax of a tragic narrative — the moment of highest tension.
exercises.answer: Catharsis is the emotional purging — of pity and fear — that Aristotle claimed the audience experiences after witnessing tragedy; it follows the climax rather than constituting it.
exercises.explanation: La catarsis es el efecto emocional en el lector/espectador, no el punto de máxima tensión narrativa.

exercises.question: Intertextuality means that a text is entirely original and independent from all previous literary works.
exercises.answer: Intertextuality means that every text is in dialogue with previous works — whether explicitly through allusion or implicitly through shared conventions.
exercises.explanation: La intertextualidad sostiene que ningún texto es completamente original ni independiente de la tradición literaria.

exercises.question: Jane Austen uses free ___ discourse — blending the narrator's voice with characters' thoughts — to devastating ironic effect.
exercises.answer: indirect

exercises.question: 'It was the best of times, it was the worst of times' places opposites in parallel structure — this is called ___.
exercises.answer: antithesis

exercises.question: The reader knows the protagonist is doomed before she does — this creates ___ irony.
exercises.answer: dramatic

exercises.question: The recurring image of water in the novel functions as a ___, accumulating symbolic weight through repetition.
exercises.answer: motif

exercises.question: The character whose contrasting traits highlight the protagonist's hesitance is called a ___.
exercises.answer: foil

exercises.question: Opening images of rotting wood, unexplained shadows, and cryptic warnings are all examples of ___.
exercises.answer: foreshadowing

exercises.question: The final section of a narrative where all conflicts are resolved is called the ___.
exercises.answer: denouement

exercises.question: Quoting Shakespeare in a scene about a corporate boardroom creates ___ — a text's dialogue with an earlier canonical work.
exercises.answer: intertextuality

exercises.question: The hidden layer of meaning beneath the characters' surface conversation is called the ___.
exercises.answer: subtext

exercises.question: The protagonist's sudden recognition of who she truly is constitutes the novel's central ___.
exercises.answer: epiphany

exercises.question: La ironía dramática exige que el lector aguante la incomodidad de saber lo que el protagonista ignora.
exercises.answer: Dramatic irony demands that the reader endure the discomfort of knowing what the protagonist does not.

exercises.question: El humor deadpan no pide la risa del público; la risa llega precisamente porque no se pide.
exercises.answer: Deadpan humour does not ask for the audience's laughter; the laughter comes precisely because it is not asked for.

exercises.question: El bathos — el descenso abrupto de lo grandioso a lo trivial — es la técnica preferida de los escritores que desconfían del patetismo.
exercises.answer: Bathos — the abrupt descent from the grandiose to the trivial — is the preferred technique of writers who distrust pathos.

exercises.question: El humor negro reconoce la monstruosidad de la realidad y la rodea de chistes en lugar de mirarla de frente.
exercises.answer: Black humour acknowledges the monstrousness of reality and surrounds it with jokes rather than facing it directly.

exercises.question: La subestimación británica consiste en decir menos cuando más se espera: 'un pequeño inconveniente' en lugar de 'una catástrofe'.
exercises.answer: British understatement consists of saying less when more is expected: 'a minor inconvenience' instead of 'a catastrophe'.

exercises.question: La parodia no puede existir sin una comprensión íntima de la obra que imita: burlar bien requiere entender bien.
exercises.answer: Parody cannot exist without intimate understanding of the work it imitates: to mock well requires understanding well.

exercises.question: La teoría de la incongruencia del humor sostiene que la risa es la respuesta cognitiva a una expectativa violada.
exercises.answer: The incongruity theory of humour holds that laughter is the cognitive response to a violated expectation.

exercises.question: El humor autodespreciativo desactiva la hostilidad del público al anticiparse a la crítica y convertirla en espectáculo.
exercises.answer: Self-deprecating humour disarms audience hostility by anticipating the criticism and turning it into performance.

exercises.question: La ironía verbal — decir una cosa y significar otra — requiere mayor competencia cultural para decodificarse correctamente.
exercises.answer: Verbal irony — saying one thing and meaning another — requires the greatest cultural competence to decode correctly.

exercises.question: El sarcasmo puede ser la deshonestidad intelectual más aceptada: afirmamos lo contrario de lo que pensamos y llamamos a eso agudeza.
exercises.answer: Sarcasm may be the most socially accepted form of intellectual dishonesty: we say the opposite of what we think and call it wit.

exercises.question: Sarcasm and irony are the same: both involve saying exactly what you mean in a clear and direct way.
exercises.answer: Sarcasm is a form of irony in which the speaker says the opposite of what they mean, typically with a mocking or hostile tone.
exercises.explanation: Ironía = decir lo contrario de lo que se piensa; sarcasmo = ironía con intención burlona.

exercises.question: Deadpan comedy is defined by the performer's exaggerated facial expressions, which heighten the comedic effect.
exercises.answer: Deadpan comedy is defined by the performer's complete absence of facial expression, which heightens the comedic effect through contrast.
exercises.explanation: El deadpan funciona porque el comediante no muestra emoción alguna.

exercises.question: A Modest Proposal by Jonathan Swift is a parody of economic essays of the time.
exercises.answer: A Modest Proposal by Jonathan Swift is a satire of British colonial policy — not a parody, which would imitate the style of a specific existing work.
exercises.explanation: La sátira critica la sociedad; la parodia imita el estilo de una obra específica.

exercises.question: Bathos occurs when a narrative builds relentlessly toward a powerful and grand climax.
exercises.answer: Bathos occurs when a narrative suddenly drops from something grand or serious to something trivial — the opposite of building to a climax.
exercises.explanation: El bathos es lo opuesto al clímax: un descenso abrupto de lo elevado a lo ridículo.

exercises.question: Black humour is humorous because it avoids any engagement with dark or disturbing subject matter.
exercises.answer: Black humour is humorous precisely because it engages directly with dark or taboo subjects, using comedy as a way of processing them.
exercises.explanation: El humor negro trata temas oscuros de forma cómica, no los evita.

exercises.question: Dramatic irony occurs when a character says one thing while meaning another.
exercises.answer: Verbal irony occurs when a character says one thing while meaning another; dramatic irony occurs when the audience knows something the character does not.
exercises.explanation: Ironía verbal = lo contrario de lo que se dice; ironía dramática = el lector sabe algo que el personaje ignora.

exercises.question: The incongruity theory of humour holds that laughter arises from the satisfaction of confirmed expectations.
exercises.answer: The incongruity theory of humour holds that laughter arises from violated expectations — the gap between what we expect and what actually occurs.
exercises.explanation: La incongruencia viola, no confirma, las expectativas.

exercises.question: Parody requires no understanding of the original work — only the ability to imitate superficial features.
exercises.answer: Effective parody requires deep familiarity with the original work — only by understanding its conventions can a parodist successfully subvert them.
exercises.explanation: La parodia efectiva surge del conocimiento profundo, no de la imitación superficial.

exercises.question: Situational irony occurs when a character deliberately says the opposite of what they mean.
exercises.answer: Verbal irony occurs when a character deliberately says the opposite of what they mean; situational irony occurs when events turn out contrary to what was expected.
exercises.explanation: Ironía situacional = circunstancias inesperadas; ironía verbal = decir lo contrario de lo que se piensa.

exercises.question: Gallows humour is a form of humour that celebrates death and disaster as positive events.
exercises.answer: Gallows humour acknowledges death and disaster but uses comedy as a coping mechanism — it finds laughter in adversity without celebrating it.
exercises.explanation: El humor de horca afronta las tragedias cómicamente sin glorificarlas.

exercises.question: A comedian who delivers absurd observations with a completely flat, expressionless face is using ___ humour.
exercises.answer: deadpan

exercises.question: Saying 'the airline's fourteen-hour delay was a minor inconvenience' is a classic example of ___.
exercises.answer: understatement

exercises.question: A novel that ridicules political corruption through animal characters representing politicians is an example of ___.
exercises.answer: satire

exercises.question: The audience's awareness that the protagonist is being deceived by someone she trusts creates ___ irony.
exercises.answer: dramatic

exercises.question: Making an audience laugh by abruptly dropping from an intense emotional scene to something trivial is a deliberate use of ___.
exercises.answer: bathos

exercises.question: Jokes about mortality used as a psychological coping mechanism are categorised as ___ humour.
exercises.answer: black

exercises.question: A text that imitates Hemingway's minimalist prose in an exaggerated way for comic effect is a ___ of Hemingway.
exercises.answer: parody

exercises.question: The incongruity between what is expected and what happens — a health food shop run by people with terrible habits — produces ___ irony.
exercises.answer: situational

exercises.question: Oscar Wilde's elegant, pointed, and slightly wounding quips exemplify ___ wit: sharply critical but always sophisticated.
exercises.answer: acerbic

exercises.question: A pun exploits the multiple ___ of a word — different definitions or similar sounds — for humorous effect.
exercises.answer: meanings

exercises.question: El lenguaje jurídico utiliza la nominalización y la voz pasiva para crear un efecto de objetividad e impersonalidad.
exercises.answer: Legal language uses nominalisation and the passive voice to create an effect of objectivity and impersonality.

exercises.question: La atenuación en el discurso académico no es debilidad sino precisión: afirmar solo lo que la evidencia justifica.
exercises.answer: Hedging in academic discourse is not weakness but precision: asserting only what the evidence justifies.

exercises.question: El lenguaje corporativo ha desarrollado un vocabulario de circunloquios que disfraza la evasión como sofisticación.
exercises.answer: Corporate language has developed a vocabulary of circumlocutions that disguises evasion as sophistication.

exercises.question: Convertir un verbo en sustantivo —'investigar' en 'la investigación de'— es la nominalización característica del registro formal.
exercises.answer: Converting a verb into a noun — 'to investigate' into 'the investigation of' — is the nominalisation characteristic of formal register.

exercises.question: El lenguaje diplomático atenúa sistemáticamente cualquier posición que pudiera interpretarse como un ultimátum.
exercises.answer: Diplomatic language systematically hedges any position that could be interpreted as an ultimatum.

exercises.question: La prosa llana exige la valentía de decir las cosas directamente en lugar de escudarse en la complejidad aparente.
exercises.answer: Plain prose demands the courage to say things directly rather than sheltering behind apparent complexity.

exercises.question: Las cláusulas tipo en los contratos estandarizan la relación entre las partes para reducir la incertidumbre jurídica.
exercises.answer: Boilerplate clauses in contracts standardise the relationship between parties to reduce legal uncertainty.

exercises.question: La sección de metodología debe detallar el procedimiento con suficiente precisión para permitir la replicación del estudio.
exercises.answer: The methodology section must detail the procedure with sufficient precision to allow replication of the study.

exercises.question: Traducir un informe técnico al lenguaje accesible para el público general es una forma de mediación lingüística.
exercises.answer: Translating a technical report into language accessible to the general public is a form of linguistic mediation.

exercises.question: El registro parlamentario admite el ataque político solo dentro de las convenciones formales que gobiernan el debate.
exercises.answer: Parliamentary register permits political attack only within the formal conventions that govern the debate.

exercises.question: Nominalisation should always be avoided because it is a sign of poor writing.
exercises.answer: Nominalisation is appropriate in formal and academic writing, where it adds precision and creates the required impersonal tone; it becomes problematic only when used to the point of obscuring meaning.
exercises.explanation: La nominalización es una herramienta válida en el registro formal; el exceso es el problema.

exercises.question: Using 'at this point in time' instead of 'now' makes a sentence more formal and precise.
exercises.answer: Using 'at this point in time' instead of 'now' is an example of circumlocution — it adds no precision and should be replaced with 'now' even in formal writing.
exercises.explanation: 'At this point in time' es un circunloquio que no añade información.

exercises.question: Claiming 'this proves conclusively that X causes Y' is appropriate in academic writing when the findings are strong.
exercises.answer: In academic writing, 'this suggests a possible relationship between X and Y' is more appropriate even for strong findings — certainty claims must match the evidence.
exercises.explanation: El hedging académico exige que la fuerza de las afirmaciones refleje la fuerza de la evidencia.

exercises.question: Jargon should never appear in professional writing because it alienates readers.
exercises.answer: Jargon is appropriate in professional writing intended for specialist audiences; it should be explained or avoided only when writing for general audiences.
exercises.explanation: La jerga es una herramienta de precisión dentro de comunidades de especialistas.

exercises.question: An executive summary should reproduce the most important sections of a report verbatim for accuracy.
exercises.answer: An executive summary should distil the key findings and recommendations in the writer's own words — verbatim reproduction defeats the purpose.
exercises.explanation: El resumen ejecutivo condensa y sintetiza; no copia.

exercises.question: Diplomatic language is maximally direct to avoid misunderstanding in high-stakes negotiations.
exercises.answer: Diplomatic language is deliberately indirect and hedged to preserve deniability, avoid offence, and maintain space for negotiation.
exercises.explanation: La diplomacia requiere atenuación para proteger las relaciones y preservar salidas negociadas.

exercises.question: The passive voice is inappropriate in all formal writing because it introduces personal agency.
exercises.answer: The passive voice is widely used in formal writing precisely because it removes personal agency, creating an objective, impersonal tone.
exercises.explanation: La voz pasiva crea distancia objetiva; es muy valorada en textos académicos y legales.

exercises.question: Hedging language such as 'it seems' should be avoided in academic writing because it makes arguments sound weak.
exercises.answer: Hedging language such as 'it seems' is essential in academic writing because it accurately represents the degree of certainty the evidence supports.
exercises.explanation: El hedging es precisión epistemológica, no debilidad argumentativa.

exercises.question: A précis is longer than the original text because it includes the writer's own analysis and commentary.
exercises.answer: A précis is shorter than the original — typically one-third of its length — and contains only the original ideas, not the writer's commentary.
exercises.explanation: El précis condensa; nunca amplía ni añade perspectiva propia.

exercises.question: Plain language movements advocate replacing all technical terminology with everyday words in all documents.
exercises.answer: Plain language movements advocate replacing unnecessarily complex or bureaucratic language with clearer alternatives; they do not eliminate necessary technical terminology in specialist contexts.
exercises.explanation: El lenguaje llano elimina la complejidad innecesaria, no la precisión técnica necesaria.

exercises.question: Standard contractual clauses used in every contract without modification — such as force majeure clauses — are called ___ text.
exercises.answer: boilerplate

exercises.question: The section of an academic paper that provides a 150-250 word overview of the research question, method, and findings is the ___.
exercises.answer: abstract

exercises.question: Corporate phrases like 'operationalise synergies' and 'leverage core competencies' are examples of ___ that obscure rather than communicate.
exercises.answer: jargon

exercises.question: 'The results indicate that there may be a correlation' — the phrase 'may be' is an example of ___ language.
exercises.answer: hedging

exercises.question: Changing 'we investigated the samples' to 'the samples were investigated' uses the ___ voice to remove the agent.
exercises.answer: passive

exercises.question: Converting 'to fail' into 'the failure of', or 'to decide' into 'the decision regarding' is called ___.
exercises.answer: nominalisation

exercises.question: The brief section at the beginning of a business report that summarises key findings for senior readers is called an ___ summary.
exercises.answer: executive

exercises.question: In British formal correspondence, if you don't know the recipient's name, you begin 'Dear Sir/Madam' and close 'Yours ___'.
exercises.answer: faithfully

exercises.question: Using many words where a few would suffice — 'due to the fact that' instead of 'because' — is called ___.
exercises.answer: circumlocution

exercises.question: The ability to recognise which level of formality is appropriate for a given audience and purpose is called ___ awareness.
exercises.answer: register

exercises.question: Andarse por las ramas cuando hay que tomar decisiones difíciles es una señal de liderazgo débil.
exercises.answer: Beating around the bush when difficult decisions need to be made is a sign of weak leadership.

exercises.question: El ministro enterró el hacha de guerra con su rival tras años de disputas y llegaron a un acuerdo histórico.
exercises.answer: The minister buried the hatchet with his rival after years of disputes and reached a historic agreement.

exercises.question: Tirar la toalla demasiado pronto es el error más costoso que puede cometer un emprendedor.
exercises.answer: Throwing in the towel too soon is the most costly mistake an entrepreneur can make.
alternatives: Giving up too soon is the most costly mistake an entrepreneur can make.

exercises.question: Si sigues pateando el bote, el problema seguirá creciendo hasta que sea demasiado tarde para resolverlo.
exercises.answer: If you keep kicking the can down the road, the problem will keep growing until it's too late to solve it.

exercises.question: La connotación negativa de 'barato' frente a la neutralidad de 'económico' ilustra cómo la selección de palabras revela actitudes.
exercises.answer: The negative connotation of 'cheap' versus the neutrality of 'inexpensive' illustrates how word selection reveals attitudes.

exercises.question: Leer entre líneas es una habilidad esencial para entender la política más allá de sus comunicados oficiales.
exercises.answer: Reading between the lines is an essential skill for understanding politics beyond its official communications.

exercises.question: Quemar puentes con tus colaboradores por una victoria táctica puede costarte alianzas estratégicas a largo plazo.
exercises.answer: Burning bridges with your collaborators for a tactical victory may cost you strategic alliances in the long term.

exercises.question: Hacer la vista gorda ante la corrupción institucional es, en sí misma, una forma de corrupción.
exercises.answer: Turning a blind eye to institutional corruption is, in itself, a form of corruption.

exercises.question: El proyecto está en terreno peligroso: el presupuesto se ha triplicado y aún no hay un producto final visible.
exercises.answer: The project is on thin ice: the budget has tripled and there is still no visible final product.

exercises.question: Tomar con pinzas las estadísticas publicadas por un gobierno en campaña electoral es una actitud epistemológicamente saludable.
exercises.answer: Taking with a grain of salt the statistics published by a government in electoral campaign is an epistemologically healthy attitude.
alternatives: Taking the statistics published by a government during an electoral campaign with a grain of salt is an epistemologically healthy attitude.

exercises.question: She burned her bridges by maintaining excellent relationships with everyone she had previously worked with.
exercises.answer: She burned her bridges by damaging her relationships with everyone she had previously worked with — she can no longer count on their support.
exercises.explanation: 'Burn bridges' = destruir relaciones, no mantenerlas.

exercises.question: 'Let the cat out of the bag' means to carefully guard a secret over a long period of time.
exercises.answer: 'Let the cat out of the bag' means to accidentally reveal a secret that was supposed to be kept hidden.
exercises.explanation: Irse de la lengua / revelar accidentalmente un secreto, no guardarlo.

exercises.question: The verb 'throw in the towel' describes an enthusiastic start to a difficult project.
exercises.answer: The idiom 'throw in the towel' describes giving up — admitting defeat in a difficult situation.
exercises.explanation: Tirar la toalla = rendirse, no iniciar algo con entusiasmo.

exercises.question: Saying a politician 'sat on the fence' means they took a strong, decisive position on every issue.
exercises.answer: Saying a politician 'sat on the fence' means they avoided committing to a clear position on any issue.
exercises.explanation: Sentarse en la valla = evitar comprometerse, no tomar posición.

exercises.question: 'Tenacious', 'stubborn', and 'obstinate' are perfect synonyms with no meaningful difference in connotation.
exercises.answer: 'Tenacious' carries a positive connotation of admirable persistence; 'stubborn' is neutral to negative; 'obstinate' implies unreasonable inflexibility and is more negative still.
exercises.explanation: Los sinónimos parciales difieren en connotación; este es un punto clave del nivel C2.

exercises.question: The phrase 'cut corners' has a positive connotation, suggesting efficiency and finding smarter ways of working.
exercises.answer: The phrase 'cut corners' has a negative connotation, implying that standards were compromised or proper procedures were skipped to save time or money.
exercises.explanation: 'Cut corners' = hacer las cosas a medias / saltarse procedimientos; connotación negativa.

exercises.question: In English, you can 'do' a decision just as naturally as 'make' a decision — both are equally acceptable.
exercises.answer: In English, the natural collocation is 'make a decision', not 'do a decision' — learners must acquire the conventional pairings that native speakers use automatically.
exercises.explanation: Las colocaciones no siguen reglas lógicas; deben aprenderse como unidades fijas.

exercises.question: Idiomatic expressions are fully appropriate in all registers, including formal academic writing.
exercises.answer: Idiomatic expressions should be avoided in formal academic writing, where precision and register consistency are required; they are appropriate in journalistic, informal, and conversational registers.
exercises.explanation: Las expresiones idiomáticas son informales; en textos académicos se prefiere el lenguaje preciso.

exercises.question: 'Bite the bullet' means to delay an unpleasant decision until the very last possible moment.
exercises.answer: 'Bite the bullet' means to accept and endure an unpleasant but necessary situation — acting decisively despite discomfort, not delaying.
exercises.explanation: Morder la bala = afrontar algo difícil con estoicismo, no posponerlo.

exercises.question: 'Getting the ball rolling' is best used to describe concluding or summarising a meeting or event.
exercises.answer: 'Getting the ball rolling' describes initiating or starting a process — not concluding it.
exercises.explanation: Poner la pelota en movimiento = empezar/arrancar, no concluir.

exercises.question: After twenty minutes of avoiding the central question, the interviewer asked the politician to stop ___ around the bush.
exercises.answer: beating

exercises.question: The two rival companies finally ___ the hatchet and announced a joint venture.
exercises.answer: buried

exercises.question: She had one last argument saved for the right moment — an ace up her ___.
exercises.answer: sleeve

exercises.question: The manager asked everyone to stop kicking the can down the ___ and make a final decision.
exercises.answer: road

exercises.question: Despite all the setbacks, she managed to ___ the storm and deliver the project on time.
exercises.answer: weather

exercises.question: The natural word pairing 'make a decision' rather than 'do a decision' is an example of ___.
exercises.answer: collocation

exercises.question: After the first prototype failed, the engineering team had no choice but to go back to the drawing ___.
exercises.answer: board

exercises.question: The opposition accused the government of ___ a blind eye to corporate tax avoidance for years.
exercises.answer: turning

exercises.question: The negotiation went well until the client tried to move the ___ posts at the eleventh hour.
exercises.answer: goal

exercises.question: Calling someone 'tenacious' is more ___ than calling them 'stubborn', which implies unreasonableness.
exercises.answer: positive

exercises.question: La síntesis exige algo más que la suma de sus partes: hay que identificar cómo las fuentes se articulan, contradicen o complementan.
exercises.answer: Synthesis demands more than the sum of its parts: you must identify how different sources relate to, contradict, or complement one another.

exercises.question: La mediación lingüística es la habilidad de transferir significado de un texto a otro contexto sin traicionarlo.
exercises.answer: Linguistic mediation is the skill of transferring meaning from one text to another context without betraying it.

exercises.question: La paráfrasis efectiva no reorganiza las palabras del original; las reemplaza con otras que expresen el mismo significado de forma diferente.
exercises.answer: An effective paraphrase does not reorganise the original's words; it replaces them with others that express the same meaning differently.

exercises.question: La competencia pragmática es la capacidad de elegir no solo las palabras correctas sino la estrategia comunicativa adecuada al contexto.
exercises.answer: Pragmatic competence is the ability to choose not only the right words but the communicative strategy appropriate to the context.

exercises.question: La evaluación crítica de una fuente va más allá de lo que dice: examina cómo lo dice, por qué, y qué supuestos da por sentados.
exercises.answer: The critical evaluation of a source goes beyond what it says: it examines how it says it, why, and what assumptions it takes for granted.

exercises.question: La fluidez sin exactitud produce malentendidos; la exactitud sin fluidez produce comunicación árida e ineficaz.
exercises.answer: Fluency without accuracy produces misunderstandings; accuracy without fluency produces arid and ineffective communication.

exercises.question: La coherencia discursiva es la capacidad de construir significado acumulativo a través del texto, más allá de la corrección gramatical.
exercises.answer: Discourse coherence is the ability to build cumulative meaning across a text, beyond mere grammatical correctness.

exercises.question: La mediación cultural exige que el mediador comprenda no solo dos lenguas sino dos formas de ver el mundo.
exercises.answer: Cultural mediation demands that the mediator understand not only two languages but two ways of seeing the world.

exercises.question: Un lector de nivel C2 no se conforma con el significado literal: lee la connotación, el subtexto, la ironía y la ideología del texto.
exercises.answer: A C2-level reader is not satisfied with literal meaning: they read the connotation, subtext, irony, and ideology of the text.

exercises.question: Dominar una lengua es poder usarla para pensar, no solo para comunicar.
exercises.answer: To master a language is to be able to use it for thinking, not merely for communicating.

exercises.question: A précis reproduces the key sentences of the original text verbatim to preserve the author's exact meaning.
exercises.answer: A précis restates the key ideas in the writer's own words — direct quotation undermines the purpose of demonstrating comprehension and synthesis.
exercises.explanation: El précis demuestra comprensión activa; copiar frases del original no cumple esa función.

exercises.question: Linguistic mediation is simply a synonym for translation from one language to another.
exercises.answer: Linguistic mediation encompasses a broader range of tasks than translation — including summarising, paraphrasing, adapting register, and explaining cultural references, often within a single language.
exercises.explanation: La mediación lingüística es más amplia que la traducción interlingüística.

exercises.question: Register conversion requires changing only the vocabulary of a text, not its structure or tone.
exercises.answer: Register conversion requires changing vocabulary, sentence structure, degree of formality, tone, and sometimes the degree of directness — it is a holistic transformation.
exercises.explanation: La conversión de registro es holística; no se limita al vocabulario.

exercises.question: Synthesis is equivalent to summary: both involve condensing multiple sources into fewer words.
exercises.answer: Synthesis goes beyond summary by integrating ideas from multiple sources to build a coherent argument that shows how the sources relate to, contradict, or build on each other.
exercises.explanation: La síntesis construye; el resumen solo condensa.

exercises.question: A C2 learner's goal is to achieve a native-like accent and eliminate all traces of their first language.
exercises.answer: A C2 learner's goal is to communicate with precision, stylistic range, and cultural sensitivity — not necessarily to eliminate an accent, which is neither required nor always achievable or desirable.
exercises.explanation: El nivel C2 es de dominio comunicativo, no de eliminación de acento.

exercises.question: When paraphrasing, you should change as few words as possible to stay close to the original.
exercises.answer: When paraphrasing, you should substantially change both vocabulary and structure while preserving meaning — merely replacing individual words is not genuine paraphrase.
exercises.explanation: La paráfrasis requiere transformación real, no sustitución superficial de palabras.

exercises.question: Discourse coherence is achieved through correct grammar alone.
exercises.answer: Discourse coherence is achieved through cohesive devices, appropriate pronoun reference, logical idea ordering, and maintained topic focus — grammar is necessary but not sufficient.
exercises.explanation: La coherencia discursiva va mucho más allá de la corrección gramatical.

exercises.question: A critical evaluation should conclude with a clear statement of whether the source is 'good' or 'bad'.
exercises.answer: A critical evaluation should assess the source's strengths and limitations with respect to specific criteria — purpose, methodology, evidence, and assumptions — rather than reduce it to a binary judgement.
exercises.explanation: La evaluación crítica es matizada; no reduce los textos a categorías binarias.

exercises.question: Pragmatic precision means using grammatically correct sentences in all communicative contexts.
exercises.answer: Pragmatic precision means choosing the communicative strategy, degree of directness, and linguistic form appropriate to the specific context, relationship, and purpose — grammatical correctness is only one component.
exercises.explanation: La precisión pragmática es más que gramática; incluye estrategia comunicativa y adecuación contextual.

exercises.question: Automaticity in language production means never making any errors.
exercises.answer: Automaticity means producing language with minimal conscious effort — even C2 speakers make occasional performance errors, but these arise from processing load, not systemic gaps in competence.
exercises.explanation: La automaticidad es eficiencia de procesamiento; los errores de actuación son normales incluso en hablantes nativos.

exercises.question: Rewriting 'The government has implemented significant austerity measures' informally: 'The government has ___ major cuts'.
exercises.answer: made

exercises.question: The opening section of an academic article that states the research question, method, findings, and conclusions is the ___.
exercises.answer: abstract

exercises.question: Integrating ideas from five different academic sources into a single coherent argument is an act of ___.
exercises.answer: synthesis

exercises.question: When you explain a complex statistical report to a non-specialist audience using accessible language, you are performing linguistic ___.
exercises.answer: mediation

exercises.question: To ___ is to restate an idea in different words while preserving the original meaning — a key skill in the C2 précis task.
exercises.answer: paraphrase

exercises.question: The ability to adjust language, tone, and strategy to suit any audience demonstrates a wide ___ range.
exercises.answer: stylistic

exercises.question: Recognising that 'I'll bear your suggestion in mind' probably means 'no' in a formal meeting demonstrates ___ competence.
exercises.answer: pragmatic

exercises.question: When a translated text resonates naturally for the target audience culturally, the translator has achieved successful ___ mediation.
exercises.answer: cultural

exercises.question: A writer who can produce a sonnet, a legal contract, a satirical column, and an academic essay with equal facility demonstrates exceptional ___ range.
exercises.answer: stylistic

exercises.question: Connecting ideas within a text using expressions like 'furthermore', 'nevertheless', and 'by contrast' are called ___ devices.
exercises.answer: cohesive
